spans.text: The [&] Protocol
An open, language-agnostic specification for declaring and composing what an agent can
do
six
cognitive primitives combine through two operators whose meaning
is fixed by the
governance kernel
. [&] does not replace MCP or A2A —
it
compiles into them
, with a certificate for every verdict.
The six primitives
Each primitive is a typed interface; a provider implements it. Declaring
&memory
says the agent has a memory faculty obeying the memory contract — not which engine backs it.
&memory — retrieve, route, store, learn, consolidate.   provider · Graphonomous
&reason — argue, vote, credit, seal; routed to on a known-unknown.   provider · Deliberatic
&time — anomaly detection, forecasting, horizon obligations.   provider · TickTickClock
&space — location, geo-routing, delta-CRDT state sync.   provider · GeoFleetic
&body — perception, typed action, affordance enumeration.   spec · Embodiment (OS-011)
&govern — the kernel itself, as a primitive.   provider · box-and-box
Two operators
combines capabilities into a coalition (associative, commutative, idempotent).
pipelines them into a governed sequence, gated by feasibility. The operators have
laws
, and the laws are property-tested — that’s what separates [&] from an ad-hoc DSL.
